newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes higher on late supply.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes higher on late supply.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed 10 basis points higher at 23.10 percent on Thursday, as dealers dumped paper just before the close, as they have in other recent sessions, traders said.
"The session was hallmarked by thin volume and speculation. They tried to jack rates up early on, but it stuck at around 22.75 percent for most of the session," said a trader.
"Then those who had hung on to paper, in the hope of selling it at lower rates, sold it anyway towards the close," he added.
The overnight Cetes rate closed at a session high after trading as low as 22.35 percent during the session.
"We're beginning to see term paper in supply, which could be a sign that rates should not come down any further," a trader said.
Some traders pointed to political uncertainty as a factor that could rein in the recent trend toward lower rates.
"Although the market is calm at the moment, we have to take into account that the ARE (Alliance for Economic Recovery) is due for renewal and U.S. elections are coming up," said a trader.
The ARE is an economic pact between labor and business leaders and the government.
